content.text: {"headline":"Approve P4 (overtime + delayed breaks + callback + chat deflection): the only option predicted to reach the 80% target, at 81.5% for 13:45-15:45, extra cost INR 3,336.","why":"General is short on agents because of a sick wave. It has 26.1 agents on the phones against 32 planned, and 6 agents went home unwell after lunch. Call volume and handle time are normal, so this is a capacity problem. With no action, service level is predicted at 62.9% for 13:45-15:45, with 9.0% abandons. P4 combines offering overtime to 22 agents (12 General, 10 Payments) for 14:15-15:15, delaying breaks by 45 min, IVR callback, and 20% chat deflection on simple enquiries. It is the only plan predicted to clear 80%: 81.5% overall, abandons down to 3.4%, and rest of day 91.3% versus 83.5% with no action. It breaks no policy and needs no escalation.","trade_offs":["Cost: P4 adds INR 3,336. The cheaper options fall short of target: P3 costs INR 816 and reaches 73.5%, P2 costs INR 2,520 and reaches 72.8%.","Customer impact: abandons fall from 9.0% to 3.4%. P3 gets to 5.7%. P1 costs nothing but does slightly worse than no action (60.8%), so it is not worth doing alone.","Other queue: Payments stays the weaker queue under P4 at 78.5%, just under target on its own, while General reaches 85.5%. The 80% target is met on the combined figure only.","Risk: P4 depends on enough agents accepting overtime. If uptake is low, the result will drift toward P3's 73.5%."],"watch":"Track overtime acceptance before 14:15 and Payments service level each interval. If uptake is short or Payments stays below about 78%, consider widening chat deflection or the callback window. Also watch for further sick-home logs after 13:42."}
